title: Chance-Safe Minimax Value for Tied Dynamic Regimes under a Budget Constraint
banked_reason: Stage 0.5 (typed) BELOW NOVELTY FLOOR: tier=incremental < floor=field and NOT salvageable in scope; math panel PASS and cited source verified.
gap_reasons: D0.5.G tier=incremental < floor=field (target=field) and NOT salvageable in scope
The Gaussian game itself receives a qualitative ten-dimensional discretization theorem, but the paper never computes a certified interval for that full value

The fixed three-regime, fixed-baseline construction, absent full-game computation, and unsupported all-rule converse leave the package as a narrow methodological note rather than a field-level result.
proof_attempt_summary: D0 built a value-preserving 21-to-10 score reduction, a qualitative rational certificate scheme, and an analytic two-point lower bound; the math panel passed and the Hirano-Porter source was verified. D0.5 nevertheless calibrated the package as incremental against the field floor, with no executed full-game interval and an unresolved paper-owned compact-action LAN transfer concern in the general review. A future field-level project would need a new research anchor plus the stronger transfer and computed full-game certificates.
tldr: At an interior stylized two-stage training design, two active dynamic regimes tie in welfare and expected subsidy cost while a no-treatment regime provides a reserve. The paper derives the sharp full-observation chance-safe value for all data-dependent rules over the fixed randomized mixture class, proves equality with the finite causal experiment, gives a value-preserving reduction of the continuum certificate from twenty-one score coordinates to ten, and constructs an attaining observed-data rule. Determinate but generally exponential finite programs give convergent certified lower and upper bounds without an endpoint-gap rate. A Fisher-minimal common-cost subexperiment supplies an explicit positive global lower bound and shows why whole-cohort regime selection has divergent scaled regret; whether the ten-coordinate experiment can be compressed to the three tangent coordinates remains open.
gap: Dynamic policy-learning papers bound welfare regret and budget excess, while local treatment-choice papers compute Gaussian minimax decisions without an estimated binding fiscal constraint. Neither literature solves an unrestricted rule problem with a continuum of strict chance-safety constraints.
fill: The project identifies the exact constrained Gaussian value, proves its equivalence to the finite causal experiment, and makes the value and an attaining rule qualitatively auditable for rational or computable \(R\) through explicit convergent lower and upper programs.
